Aisha told Sa'd b. Hisham the Prophet's character was the Quran, night prayer became voluntary after a year, and described his witr of nine, later seven, rak'ahs.
When illness or sleep kept the Prophet from night prayer he prayed twelve rak'ahs by day, and a night portion of Quran missed is recorded if recited before noon.
The Prophet said the prayer of the penitent is observed when young weaned camels feel the heat of the sun.
Night prayer is offered in pairs of rak'ahs, and one fearing dawn adds a single rak'ah; witr is one rak'ah at the end of the night prayer, prayed before morning.
Night prayer is in pairs closed by one rak'ah; observe witr before morning, early if one may not wake, otherwise at the end of the night, which is witnessed.
The most excellent prayer is the one in which the standing is longest.
Every night there is an hour in which any Muslim who asks Allah for good in this world and the next is given it.
Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven, asking who will call on Him, ask of Him or seek His forgiveness, until daybreak.
Praying at night in Ramadan or on Lailat-ul-Qadr with faith and hope of reward brings forgiveness of past sins; the Prophet stopped leading Ramadan night prayer lest it become obligatory.
Ubayy b. Ka'b swore that Lailat-ul-Qadr is in Ramadan, on the twenty-seventh night, and that the sun rises next morning bright without rays.
Spending a night at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet's night prayer, was moved from his left to his right, and heard him pray for light within and around him.
At night the Prophet recited the last verses of Al Imran, prayed thirteen rak'ahs with witr, and moved Ibn Abbas from his left to his right.
On a journey the Prophet prayed in one garment tied at opposite ends and moved Jabir, standing behind him, to his right.
The Prophet began his night prayer with two short rak'ahs and told others to do the same.
Rising to pray at night the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth and asked guidance and forgiveness, with set words for bowing and prostrating.
At night the Prophet recited al-Baqara, al-Nisa and Al Imran before bowing, pausing to glorify, ask and seek refuge, and prayed so long Abdullah thought of sitting.
The devil urinates in the ear of an all-night sleeper and ties three knots on sleepers, undone by remembrance, ablution and prayer; the Prophet urged Ali and Fatimah to pray.
Pray some prayers at home and do not make houses graves; a man's prayer at home is best except the obligatory, and Satan flees a house where al-Baqara is recited.
Allah loves best deeds done constantly, even if small; the Prophet had Zainab's prayer rope untied and, about a woman praying all night, said to do what one can sustain.
Whoever dozes in prayer, or whose tongue falters reciting the Quran at night, should sleep first, for he may not know whether he is asking pardon or reviling himself.
A man's recitation reminded the Prophet of verses he had been made to forget; keep refreshing the Quran, which escapes faster than hobbled camels, and never say 'I forgot it'.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran in a sweet voice, and Abu Musa was given a voice like those of David's family.
In the year of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath on his mount while travelling, repeating the words, as Ibn Mughaffal later demonstrated.
A cloud that frightened a horse while its owner recited al-Kahf was tranquillity descending, and the canopy of lamps over Usaid b. Hudair as he recited was angels listening.
A believer who recites the Quran is like a sweet, fragrant orange; the proficient reciter is with the noble recording angels, and one who falters in it has two rewards.
Allah commanded the Prophet to recite to Ubayy, who wept at being named; the Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him and wept at a verse of Surat al-Nisa'.
In Hims Ibn Mas'ud recited Surah Yusuf, which the Prophet had approved; the man who denied it smelled of wine, so Ibn Mas'ud lashed him with the prescribed punishment.
Three verses recited in prayer, or verses taught or recited in the mosque each morning, are better than as many large she-camels.
The Quran will intercede for its reciters on Resurrection Day, and al-Baqara and Al Imran will come like two clouds or flocks of birds pleading for those who recited them.
An angel announced to the Prophet two lights given to no prophet before, the Fatiha and the end of al-Baqara, whose last two verses suffice whoever recites them at night.
Whoever learns by heart ten verses of Surah al-Kahf, from its beginning or, in one narration, its end, will be protected from the Dajjal.
Ubayy b. Ka'b named 'Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal' as the greatest verse in the Book of Allah, and the Prophet praised his knowledge.
'Say: He is Allah, One' equals a third of the Quran, and Allah loves the expedition leader who ended his recitation in prayer with it because it describes the Compassionate.
The Prophet said verses unlike any seen before had come down: the Mu'awwadhatain, 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the dawn' and 'with the Lord of men'.
Envy is justified only of two: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, or wisdom he judges and teaches by, and one given wealth who spends it.
Umar, told that his collector had appointed a freed slave versed in the Book of Allah, quoted the Prophet: by this Book Allah exalts some peoples and degrades others.
Umar and Ubayy objected to others' different recitations, but the Prophet approved each, saying the Quran was sent down in seven modes, granted at his request to ease his people.
Ibn Mas'ud told a man who recited all the mufassal surahs in one rak'ah that he rushed like poetry, recalling how the Prophet paired surahs, two in each rak'ah.
The Prophet read 'muddakir' with a d, and Abu Darda' heard him recite 'By the night when it covers' with 'the male and the female', as Ibn Mas'ud did.
The Prophet forbade praying after the dawn prayer till sunrise, after Asr till sunset, and as the sun rises, stands at midday or sets, for it rises between Satan's horns.
